canonical_name: Klein model (source topic label; exact proposition open)
literal_source_claim_en: A projective model of hyperbolic geometry.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies no source edition, definition chain, formula, or proposition. It does not say whether the root defines a projective-ball metric, proves metric laws, characterizes chord geodesics, establishes a projective transformation group, satisfies synthetic hyperbolic axioms, proves curvature/completeness, constructs an inter-model isometry, or bundles several results. Carrier, dimension, quadratic form, affine chart, cross-ratio convention, normalization, binders, hypotheses, conclusion, and boundary cases are all open. Selecting a standard presentation would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Prospective objects include an affine open disk or ball, the interior of a real projective conic or quadric, a homogeneous-coordinate vector space and scalar quotient, a quadratic form and affine chart, boundary intersections, a normalized cross-ratio distance or other hyperbolic structure, projective transformations, geodesics, and a comparison hyperbolic geometry. Exact dimensions, universes, fields, structures, instances, coercions, and representations remain open.
conclusion: Open: the repository names a projective model but supplies no truth-valued property or conclusion bundle.
candidate_statement_shape_not_credited: Construct a source-selected projective disk or ball with a source-normalized Klein metric or incidence structure, then prove the source-selected hyperbolic-model, geodesic, symmetry, curvature, completeness, or comparison claims. The exact carrier, subset, and normalization are not selected.

alternate_encodings.target: An affine open unit ball with a source-normalized Klein distance is isometric to a hyperboloid or another selected hyperbolic-space model.
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate metric/comparison formulation requiring an explicit construction and checked transport

alternate_encodings.target: Klein-model geodesics are intersections of projective lines with the model domain and appear as Euclidean chords in an affine chart.
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate consequence or characterization, not the model theorem by title alone

alternate_encodings.target: Projective transformations preserving the boundary conic act by isometries of the Klein distance.
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate symmetry theorem requiring a source-selected group, action, and distance convention
